candidates.name: Yellowknife Bay: Sheepbed to Gillespie Lake and Point Lake
candidates.science_question: How do the locally exposed sedimentary members record changing lake and stream conditions?
observed_basis: Curiosity images document the Sheepbed mudstone and overlying Gillespie Lake and Point Lake exposures.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Compare member contacts, bedding and changes in sediment texture if covered by the selected public crop.

data_readiness.science_context: Published rover lithostratigraphy; public orbital registration pending

limitations: The source scene includes features approximately 8-30 m from the rover; it does not define a georeferenced 128 m crop.
This is a compact-station analogue, not evidence that arbitrary 128 m windows contain multiple members.

candidates.name: Pahrump Hills: exposed basal Murray outcrop
candidates.science_question: Which bedding and contact relationships can be compared within the basal sedimentary section?
observed_basis: NASA describes approximately 18 m of vertical rock exposure alongside sand ripples in the Pahrump Hills scene.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Compare bedrock-ripple boundaries and lateral changes between exposed beds; do not assume sand trafficability.
limitations: The published 18 m is vertical section thickness, not horizontal route length.
A panoramic image is not a DEM, terrain mask or accepted approach route.

candidates.name: Glen Torridon: clay-bearing trough toward Greenheugh contact
candidates.science_question: How do sedimentary facies and later alteration vary toward the pediment contact?
observed_basis: The published campaign documented lacustrine mudstones, more energetic sandstone facies and heterogeneous alteration across a 5 km traverse.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Compare cross-bedding, contact exposures and diagenetic features where public observations support them.
limitations: A 128 m station cannot represent the complete published campaign.
The selected contact window must be located and registered; no coordinate or rover reachability is inferred.

candidates.name: Mawrth Vallis: layered exposures beside a dark-mantled tributary
candidates.science_question: Can a local transect compare exposed clay-bearing horizons and the overlying dark mantle?
observed_basis: HiRISE documents approximately 1.6 km-wide hills and a stereo DTM with associated orthoimages.
Published CRISM research identifies compositionally distinct stratigraphic horizons.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Investigate mantle edges, erosional windows and bed orientations before proposing any local sample.

data_readiness.science_layer: CRISM mineral interpretation published; exact registered layer subset not imported

limitations: Best documented alternative for a data-import study; it is not an integrated public package.
The catalog center is not a proposed base, target or crop center.
If HiRISE is evaluator reference, a newly agreed public/held-out partition is required before planning with these products.

candidates.name: NE Syrtis: megabreccia and altered-unit contact sector
candidates.science_question: Which contacts distinguish ancient disrupted materials from later igneous and aqueous alteration units?
observed_basis: The JPL candidate dossier describes diverse basement, megabreccia and overlying altered units; the HiRISE catalog lists a contact-region DTM.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Inspect exposed contacts, block populations and fractures; competing alteration origins remain hypotheses.
limitations: The JPL worksheet was reviewed through indexed text; direct retrieval was unavailable.
Catalog listing alone does not establish an image/DEM/science-layer overlap.
Steep mesas and large blocks are science context, not an approved walkable transect.

candidates.name: Nili Fossae: olivine-carbonate-clay exposure in PIA11730
candidates.science_question: How are carbonate-bearing exposures related to olivine, clay-bearing substrate and the upper rock cover?
observed_basis: NASA publishes a roughly 3 km-wide CRISM/HiRISE composite showing the stratigraphic association of these materials.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Compare erosional contacts, retained cap rock and nearby sand derived from exposed materials if the crop covers them.
limitations: Mineral assignments derive from spectroscopy and interpretation, not DEM or visible color alone.
This exposure is not automatically on a route through NE Syrtis or Jezero.
Composite overlap does not yet provide the canonical terrain package or its uncertainty.

candidates.name: Eberswalde: delta-front lobe and nearby inverted distributary
candidates.science_question: Which local exposures constrain delta architecture and the relationship between channels and fine deposits?
observed_basis: The JPL worksheet describes a roughly 10 by 10 km delta with inverted channels, clay-bearing deposits and unresolved crater-floor materials.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Compare eroded lobe fronts, channel intersections and any supported contacts with impact-related or vein-bearing materials.
limitations: The DTM footprint must be checked against the selected lobe; the product center is not a mission target.
A local crop cannot represent the full delta.
HiRISE public/reference partition and new-site registration need owner agreement.

candidates.name: Holden: southwestern layered deposits below alluvial material
candidates.science_question: How do finely bedded deposits differ from the overlying alluvial cover?
observed_basis: NASA describes southwestern exposures whose beds can be followed hundreds of metres to kilometres, with spectral indications of clays.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Examine stratigraphic boundaries and lateral continuity; compare alluvial and finer layered exposures.
limitations: The 0.25 m figure is image map scale, not DEM resolution or vertical accuracy.
The breached-rim terrain does not imply a safe ingress or a feasible return.
A sector-specific public DEM and registration are pending.

candidates.name: Oxia Planum: exposed clay-bearing terrain and surviving cover contact
candidates.science_question: What relationships between clay-bearing bedrock, later cover and channel deposits can a selected local exposure resolve?
observed_basis: ESA's site-selection account describes ancient clay-bearing rocks, channel context and locally retained later cover.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Compare erosion windows and exposed cover boundaries; channel-related features require confirmed crop overlap.
limitations: No specific downloadable DTM and exact overlap were verified in this survey.
Historical ExoMars schedule text is obsolete and not part of this proposal.
A historical site-selection safety margin is not agent-specific traversability.

candidates.name: Home Plate eastern margin and silica-bearing soils
candidates.science_question: How might local exposures test the competing formation histories of silica-rich deposits?
observed_basis: Spirit's disturbed soil revealed high silica; APXS and Mini-TES measurements supported the compositional interpretation.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Inspect already exposed bright soils and nearby stratification using an explicit instrument model; do not reproduce wheel damage as a sensing requirement.
limitations: The historical discovery was incidental; a simulator must not guarantee another discovery.
Silica is not identifiable from the DEM; a declared scientific sensor/result contract is needed.
The historical hot-spring/fumarole alternatives do not establish a biosignature or a safe present approach.

candidates.name: Endurance: rim-to-exposed-section sector with dune exclusion
candidates.science_question: What stratigraphic and alteration contrasts can an accessible crater-wall sector reveal while rejecting an unsafe extension?
observed_basis: NASA records a rejected entry location and a later refusal to cross inner dunes.
Regional Opportunity research relates sedimentary and alteration observations to wind and water processes.
proposed_secondary_opportunities: Compare accessible beds and supported concretions/fractures; retain the inner dunes as a historical negative-access analogue, not a required destination.
limitations: Do not reuse Opportunity's historical route as authorization for different agents.
The inner dunes are a rejected historical extension, not an approved POI to reach.
The regional 2011 paper is not the source for the 2004 entry/dune decisions.
New public terrain, uncertainty and instrument bindings are pending.

shared_requests_to_data_owner: Select a science-feature polygon from the cited primary material before fixing a crop center.
Return actual product IDs, footprints, hashes, native DEM and image scales, horizontal/vertical references, masks and uncertainty.
Verify co-registration of DEM, image and any spectral/geological layer with independent controls.
Provide a public canonical package and preserve unknown/NoData distinctions; do not synthesize observations or evaluator values.
Retain a small operational window within wider context; map size alone does not approve longer routes, more service or larger resource budgets.
limitations: No alternative sector has been imported, georegistered, planned or executed by this artifact.
Secondary opportunities are proposed investigations, not guaranteed detections or completed tasks.
Orbital estimates and published science context do not certify local soil, traction, clearance or safe traversal.
Biosignature preservation potential does not establish ancient life.
Landing-site constraints must not be copied as universal EVA or robot safety thresholds.

ai_disclosure.use: AI-assisted primary-source synthesis and proposed crop-size alternatives; no terrain, image, observation or execution data generated
